content.text:
The setup summary card in the Agent panel is built from a fixed, hand-picked list of 13 slicer settings, not from the full settings set and not from the conversation. That explains both problems you noticed: the expanded view mostly repeats the summary, and it can never cover everything because nothing outside those 13 keys can appear except as a "change from preset". Questions 1, 2 and 4 are answered from the code; question 3 is my recommendation.

## 1. How the three lines are generated

All three are composed in [SetupCard.tsx](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx) from raw values the C++ host reads out of OrcaSlicer. No model writes any of this text.

| Line | Source | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `0.20mm Standard @MyKlipper` | [SetupCard.tsx:642](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx:642) | The title is the chat's stated purpose if the agent has recorded one, otherwise the name of the selected process preset. Here no purpose was recorded, so you see the preset name. |
| `0.20 mm layers · 3 walls` | `appliedSummary`, [SetupCard.tsx:178](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx:178) | Always `layer_height` and `wall_loops`, in that order. |
| `15% crosshatch infill · supports off` | same function | Always `sparse_infill_density` + `sparse_infill_pattern`, then `enable_support` (+ support type and "build plate only" when on). |

The four facts and their order are hard-coded; they never follow what changed last. The wording adapts in a few cases:

- **Objects disagree:** the line becomes "Plate default: … · N objects with local overrides".
- **One modifier overrides a value:** that exception is quoted inline.
- **Anything more complicated:** the line says "local … settings — see details".
- **Spiral vase mode:** both lines are replaced by "Spiral vase mode".

## 2. How the details are generated, and what decides what shows

It is not "show everything". There are four sections, each with its own rule:

- **Printer & material**: names only (printer preset, nozzle sizes, one row per filament slot, bed type). No settings from inside those presets.
- **Applied settings · Plate 1**: six rows built from the same 13-key list, `kSetupKeys` in [OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:164](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:164). Each value is resolved object → plate → process preset, so this is the value in force, edits included. Four of the six rows (layer height, walls, infill, supports) restate the summary lines; only top/bottom shells and brim are new.
- **Local overrides**: every key set on an object, modifier, part or height range, plus paint, blockers and enforcers. Only 14 keys have display names; the rest collapse to "N other local settings".
- **N changes from preset**: every process setting whose current value differs from the saved preset, with OrcaSlicer's own label and `preset → current`. This is the only uncurated list.

Two gaps follow from this:

- A process setting outside the 13 keys that is still at its preset value (speeds, seam, ironing, about 340 of the 356 process keys) is not visible anywhere on the card.
- "Changes from preset" covers the process preset only. An edited filament temperature or printer setting does not show up.

## 3. A scalable way to reach different levels of detail

My recommendation is to stop growing the inventory and organize the card by difference from the preset. An inventory grows with the 356 settings; a difference list grows only with what the person or agent changed.

1. **Summary (always visible):** keep the title and two lines as they are.
2. **Details, first level:** replace the six "Applied settings" rows with the differences from the preset, grouped under OrcaSlicer's own tab names (Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Others) and capped at about five rows with "show all N". Include filament and printer preset edits. A headline row appears only when it adds something the summary could not say, such as mixed values or a local override.
3. **Details, second level:** local overrides as one line per object, expandable.
4. **Everything else:** do not render it in the card. Offer two exits:
   - a link that opens OrcaSlicer's own process settings at the relevant tab;
   - asking the agent, which can already read any setting through its settings search tool.

The card stays a summary and never becomes a second settings editor. The cost is that a setting left at its preset value is reachable only through those two exits, which I think is the right trade.

## 4. Multiple plates

Today the line count does not multiply. The host computes the applied settings for the active plate only ([OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:677](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:677)), and the estimate is also the active plate's. Selecting another plate swaps the card's contents, and the other plates are not shown at all.

If you want all plates visible at once, repeating the card N times is not necessary. In OrcaSlicer the process preset is project-wide, so plates can differ only in:

- which objects sit on them, and those objects' overrides;
- a few per-plate keys: bed type, print sequence, spiral vase mode, filament mapping;
- the slice estimate.

So I would show the shared setup once, then one line per plate, for example "Plate 2 · spiral vase · 1 object with overrides · ~1h 10m / 23 g". A plate with nothing different shows only its estimate. Growth is one line per plate, and the full detail stays tied to the active plate.

If you want to go ahead, tell me whether to change the details view (question 3), add the per-plate lines (question 4), or both.

content.text:
The sketch above shows the setup summary card as a fixed-height card in the chat (left) and a separate setup page that holds everything else (right). All names and values in it are invented for the bed-adhesion example you raised. The two object rows with a count on the right expand and collapse.

## The summary lines: you are right, drop the hard-coded fields

Showing wall loops to someone worried about bed adhesion is noise. I withdraw "keep the two lines as they are". The replacement in the sketch:

- **Line 1 is the three preset names.** That already carries the layer height in most cases, since it is in the process preset's name ("0.20mm Standard").
- **Line 2 is what differs from those presets**, up to three items, then "+N more". With no differences it reads "No changes from presets".

The three items on line 2 are picked by a fixed rule, not by a model: changes the agent made in this chat first, newest first, then your hand edits. The data is already there: the card receives this chat's change log and each preset difference is tagged as the agent's or yours. So in the bed-adhesion chat the line shows brim and first layer, and wall loops only appear if someone changed them.

## Page or popup: I recommend a page inside the panel

- **The panel already works this way.** Its body switches between the chat, the chat list and the agent setup screens, with a Back button ([App.tsx:107](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/App.tsx:107)). A setup page is a fourth view in that switch.
- **A popup has nowhere good to live.** The panel is a web page, so an in-page popup cannot be wider than the panel; it would be a page with a worse way out. A native dialog would need a second web view or a native rebuild of the same rows.
- **A page does not block the canvas.** You can click an object in the 3D view while reading its overrides. A modal dialog would prevent that.

The cost is that the chat and the full details are not visible at the same time. The compact card covers the common case, and the sketch keeps the message box on the setup page so you can ask about a row without going back.

## What the sketch commits to

- **The card in the chat never expands.** "View setup" replaces today's inline "Setup details" toggle, so the chat is never pushed down.
- **Presets are listed by name, each with its own change count.** Filament slots using the same preset collapse into one row ("Filament 2–3").
- **Changes are grouped under OrcaSlicer's own category names.** Each setting already carries one in the slicer's definitions, so no new mapping is needed. Filament and printer edits get their own group, which the card does not show today.
- **Objects are one line each.** A line expands only if the object has overrides.
- **Plates are one line each.** This answers your earlier multi-plate question on the same page.

## Decision for you

Should the message box stay visible on the setup page? I drew it in because asking "why is this 105?" while looking at the row seems useful. The catch is that the agent's answer lands in the chat, which is hidden while the setup page is open, so sending would have to return you to the chat.

<!-- reply 2 -->
> Line 1 is the three preset names. That already carries the layer height in most cases, since it is in the process preset's name ("0.20mm Standard").

Well, this is actually not the preset full name, right? It seems like a condensed name, but how do you come from the full name to the condensed name? Even with contents name, are you sure it'll be enough room to show it in one line?

<!-- reply -->
> Line 2 is what differs from those presets, up to three items, then "+N more". With no differences it reads "No changes from presets".

content.text:
Both strings in my sketch were typed by hand, and when I measured them against OrcaSlicer's real data, neither can be produced by a rule and neither fits on one line. That is the trap you describe, and the sketch was already in it. Below is what the data supports, and the method I would use so the design cannot drift from it again.

## Preset names: three on one line does not fit

I measured every preset shipped in `resources/profiles` (lengths in characters). The card fits roughly 45 characters per line, estimated from your screenshot.

| Preset type | Count | Has an ` @printer` suffix | Full name, median / 90th pct / max | Cut at ` @`, median / 90th pct / max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Process | 2,868 | 97% | 36 / 45 / 78 | 15 / 19 / 34 |
| Filament | 5,952 | 88% | 29 / 41 / 58 | 15 / 22 / 47 |
| Printer | 1,001 | 0% | 28 / 37 / 50 | same |

- **The only rule available is "cut at ` @`".** It is a naming convention, not an API. A user preset named differently would be shown whole.
- **"MyKlipper 0.4" in my sketch had no rule behind it.** I dropped the word "nozzle" by hand. Printer names have no suffix to cut.
- **Three names joined are about 64 characters at the median**, so they do not fit. Process plus filament, both cut, is about 33 at the median and about 44 at the 90th percentile, so that pair mostly fits.

So line 1 can be process and first filament ("0.20mm Standard · Generic ABS", "+2" for more filaments), with an ellipsis on overflow. The printer and all full names go on the setup page.

OrcaSlicer also stores a short "alias" on system presets. I have not confirmed what it contains; I would check that before writing a string rule.

## Setting text: what a generic rule really produces

OrcaSlicer's definition of each setting carries a label, a unit, a type, and display names for enum values. That is enough for one generic formatter, with no per-setting code. Applied to my sketch's example:

| My hand-typed text | What the generic rule gives |
|---|---|
| "Brim 8 mm outer" | Two separate items: "Brim type: Outer brim only" and "Brim width: 8 mm" |
| "first layer 0.28 mm" | "First layer height: 0.28 mm" |
| "bed 105 °C" | "Bed temperature: 105 ℃" |
| (first layer speed) | "First layer: 25 mm/s" |

Three things break:

- **Merged phrases are not derivable.** "8 mm outer brim" combines two settings. Only a hand-written special case or a model can do that.
- **Labels are not unique.** 17 labels among the 356 process settings are shared. "Outer wall" is the label for speed, acceleration, line width and jerk; "Bed temperature" covers six plate types. The unit separates speed, acceleration and width; I have not checked that it separates all 17.
- **Three items do not fit on one line.** The three real strings above total about 70 characters.

## How I avoid the trap

1. **Formatter first, mockup second.** Write the generic formatter, run it over every process, filament and printer setting, and give you the full table to read. Mockups then use only strings from that table.
2. **No setting names in the card code.** What appears is decided by one rule over all settings: it differs from the preset, ordered by who changed it and when. A test fails if the card source mentions any setting key.
3. **A random-settings test.** Change five randomly chosen settings and assert the card lists all five with a non-empty label and value. A hard-coded field list cannot pass this.
4. **Fix ugly wording with data.** An optional table of shorter labels may improve a row. Deleting the table must leave every row still showing, with OrcaSlicer's own label.
5. **Leave the smart sentence to the agent's chat message.** "I added an 8 mm outer brim" is a judgment about what matters. The agent already writes that in the reply under the card, so the card does not need to imitate it.

## The card under those rules

Every line here comes from a rule, at the cost of looking plainer than the sketch:

```
Stop the corners lifting              purpose, or the process name if none
0.20mm Standard · Generic ABS         process and first filament, cut at " @"
Brim width             0 → 8 mm       newest agent change
Brim type   Auto → Outer brim only    next newest
+3 more changes · View setup
```

With no changes, the two rows are replaced by "No changes from presets".

If you agree, the next step is item 1: the formatter and its full output table for you to review, before any change to the card.

repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check

content.text:
The formatter is written and tested: one generic function turns any OrcaSlicer setting's raw value into display text using only that setting's own definition (type, unit, choice labels), with no setting names in the code. It produces a single line of at most 48 characters for the default value of all 652 process, filament and printer settings. The 5% random sample below (33 settings) shows the values read well, but it also exposes four problems in the labels around them. Nothing is wired into the card yet and nothing is committed.

## The sample (seed 20261008)

| Preset | Key | OrcaSlicer's label | Raw value | Shown as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| process | `interlocking_beam_width` | Interlocking beam width | `0.8` | 0.8 mm |
| process | `wipe_tower_bridging` | Maximal bridging distance | `10` | 10 mm |
| process | `spiral_finishing_flow_ratio` | Spiral finishing flow ratio | `0` | 0 |
| printer | `retraction_length` | Retraction Length | `0.8` | 0.8 mm |
| filament | `filament_cooling_before_tower` | Wipe tower cooling | `10` | 10 ℃ |
| process | `set_other_flow_ratios` | Set other flow ratios | `0` | Off |
| filament | `filament_shrink` | Shrinkage (XY) | `100%` | 100% |
| process | `timelapse_type` | Timelapse | `0` | Traditional |
| process | `overhang_reverse_threshold` | Overhang reversal threshold | `50%` | 50% |
| process | `small_perimeter_threshold` | Small perimeters threshold | `0` | 0 mm |
| process | `wiping_volumes_extruders` | Purging volumes - load/unload volumes | `70,70,70,…` (10 values) | 70 |
| process | `fuzzy_skin_octaves` | Fuzzy Skin Noise Octaves | `4` | 4 |
| process | `prime_tower_enable_framework` | Internal ribs | `0` | Off |
| process | `post_process` | Post-processing Scripts | (empty) | Empty |
| filament | `filament_density` | Density | `0` | 0 g/cm³ |
| process | `enable_tower_interface_cooldown_during_tower` | Cool down from interface boost during prime tower | `0` | Off |
| process | `lateral_lattice_angle_1` | Lateral lattice angle 1 | `-45` | -45° |
| process | `brim_width` | Brim width | `0` | 0 mm |
| process | `prime_tower_brim_width` | Brim width | `3` | 3 mm |
| printer | `machine_end_gcode` | End G-code | `M104 S0 ; turn off temperature\nG28 X0 …` | 3 lines |
| process | `internal_solid_filament_id` | Internal solid infill | `0` | 0 |
| process | `skeleton_infill_density` | Skeleton infill density | `25%` | 25% |
| process | `initial_layer_min_bead_width` | First layer minimum wall width | `85%` | 85% |
| filament | `filament_stamping_distance` | Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube | `0` | 0 |
| process | `tree_support_top_rate` | Branch Density | `30%` | 30% |
| process | `gcode_add_line_number` | Add line number | `0` | Off |
| filament | `volumetric_speed_coefficients` | Max volumetric speed multinomial coefficients | `""` | Empty |
| process | `slow_down_layers` | Number of slow layers | `0` | 0 layers |
| process | `is_infill_first` | Print infill first | `0` | Off |
| process | `xy_hole_compensation` | X-Y hole compensation | `0` | 0 mm |
| printer | `resonance_avoidance` | Resonance avoidance | `0` | Off |
| printer | `extruder_clearance_height_to_rod` | Height to rod | `40` | 40 mm |
| process | `fuzzy_skin_first_layer` | Apply fuzzy skin to first layer | `0` | Off |

## What the sample shows

**Working:**
- Units attach correctly (mm, ℃, °, g/cm³, layers).
- Switches read On/Off.
- A choice shows OrcaSlicer's own name for it ("Traditional").
- G-code is described ("3 lines"), not quoted.
- A per-filament list whose values agree collapses to one value.

**Problems, all about labels and meaning:**

1. **Two settings, one label, same unit.** `brim_width` and `prime_tower_brim_width` are both "Brim width" in mm. A row reading "Brim width 0 → 8 mm" does not say which one changed.
2. **Zero often means "off" or "automatic".** "Internal solid infill: 0", "0 layers" and "0 g/cm³" are accurate but meaningless to a reader. The definition does not record what zero means, so a generic rule cannot fix this.
3. **Some labels are too long for a row.** One is 62 characters. Rows need truncation, with the full label on hover.
4. **The category is blank more often than I said.** 18 of the 33 sampled settings have none, including all 9 filament and printer ones. My earlier claim that every setting carries a category was wrong.

Problems 1 and 4 likely have the same fix: take the group name from the layout of OrcaSlicer's settings tabs, where the prime tower's brim width sits under a prime tower heading. I have not checked how reachable that layout is from our code.

## What was tested

- **Rules:** five test cases cover numbers with units, switches, choices, lists, long text, and the "before → after" form that says the unit once ("0 → 8 mm").
- **Every real setting:** one test runs the formatter over all 652 settings; 2,635 assertions pass.
- **The guard can fail:** I broke one rule on purpose (quoting multi-line text), saw 6 failures, and restored it.
- **The header split compiles:** the two app source files that include the settings header still build.

Not tested:

- The full app was not built or run, because nothing calls the formatter yet.
- Only default values were formatted, not edited values or printers with several different nozzles.

## Files

- [SettingDisplay.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/SettingDisplay.hpp): the formatter (`display_value`, `display_change`).
- [OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp): the setting-definition helpers, moved unchanged out of [OrcaSettings.hpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaSettings.hpp) so tests can use them without the GUI.
- [test_setting_display.cpp](tests/workspace/test_setting_display.cpp) and a new `setting_display_tests` target in [tests/workspace/CMakeLists.txt](tests/workspace/CMakeLists.txt).

To draw a different sample, change the seed:

```bash
/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/print-settings-display-a02cb1/build/arm64/tests/workspace/RelWithDebInfo/setting_display_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/setting_display_tests "[.sample]" --rng-seed 7
```

## Next step

I recommend resolving problem 1 before touching the card, since an ambiguous row is worse than a missing one. That means finding out whether the settings tab's group names can be read per setting. Say if you would rather I wire the formatter into the card's "changes from preset" rows first and handle labels after.

content.text:
Noted: the setup page will have no message box. On your question: no, I described what the two lines contain but never said what makes them change. Here is the answer, checked against the code that feeds the card today.

## How updating works

The lines are not stored anywhere. The app re-sends the card's data and the page rebuilds both lines from scratch at two moments ([AgentHost.cpp:566](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp:566)):

- any change to the open project: settings, objects, plates, undo or redo, a slice finishing;
- right after the agent successfully applies a settings change or records the chat's purpose.

So there is nothing to keep in sync; the question is which events change the inputs.

## Line 1: preset names

It changes when:

- you or the agent pick a different process or filament preset;
- you switch printer, which swaps the other two with it;
- a preset is saved under a new name;
- a project is opened or replaced.

## Line 2: differences from the presets

It changes when:

- **A setting is edited**, by hand in OrcaSlicer's settings panel or by the agent: the item appears or its value updates.
- **A setting is put back to the preset's value:** the item disappears.
- **Undo or redo** restores settings: the line follows.
- **The preset is saved with the edits in it:** all items disappear and the line reads "No changes from presets", although nothing about the print changed.
- **A different preset is selected:** the differences are measured against the new one.
- **The order changes** when the agent makes a new change in this chat, since its newest change goes first.

Neither line changes when you select or move objects, switch plates, or slice. Those affect only the estimate line.

## Three things this exposed that I had not specified

1. **Saving a preset empties line 2.** That follows from "difference from preset", but it may surprise someone who just asked the agent for a brim and then saved. The alternative is to keep showing what the agent changed in this chat even after a save, which is a different rule: "changed in this chat", not "differs from preset".
2. **Order in a chat that made none of the changes.** A new chat on a project with existing edits has no change history to rank by. I would fall back to OrcaSlicer's own settings order.
3. **Per-object overrides are not in line 2.** If the agent sets five walls on one object only, that is not a preset difference. The sketch covers it with the "2 objects with overrides" count at the bottom of the card, and that count would change when the active plate changes.

Also, the app currently sends differences for the process preset only. Filament and printer differences would have to be added on the app side before line 2 can show them.

## Decision for you

Item 1 is the real choice: should line 2 mean "differs from the preset" or "changed in this chat"? I recommend "differs from the preset". It is a fact OrcaSlicer can always answer, it is the same in every chat, and it matches the "Changed from presets" section on the setup page. The agent's reply in the chat already records what it changed.

# Handoff: setup card shows differences from presets

Prepared 2026-10-08 against `jusprin-newui` lineage at commit `e3f826a83c`
(branch `claude/print-settings-display-a02cb1`).

This folder is a temporary implementation handoff. Leave it untracked: do not
commit it and do not add it to any ignore file.

## The assignment in three sentences

The setup summary card in the Agent panel currently describes a print with a
fixed list of 13 slicer settings, so it shows wall loops to someone who asked
about bed adhesion and can never show a setting outside that list. Replace
that with one rule that covers every setting: the card shows which presets are
selected and what differs from them. The long expandable details move out of
the chat onto a separate page inside the panel, so the card never pushes the
conversation down.

## Files in this folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | This document. |
| `mockup.png` | The three screens, in light and dark, rendered from `mockup.html`. Look at this first. |
| `mockup.html` | Self-contained mockup. Open in a browser to inspect elements and classes. |
| `make-mockup.py` | The script that generated `mockup.html` from the token file and the page's stylesheet. |
| `formatter.patch` | Work already done and tested: the generic value formatter and its tests. Apply it first. |

## Decisions Kenneth has made. Do not reopen them.

1. **No hard-coded setting list.** (2026-10-07) The two summary lines must not
   be fixed fields. He called the current behaviour arbitrary.
2. **The card means "differs from the preset".** (2026-10-08) Not "changed in
   this chat". A consequence he accepted: saving a preset with the edits in it
   empties the list, because nothing differs any more.
3. **Details are a page inside the panel, not an inline expansion.** He asked
   whether it should be a page or a popup; a page was recommended and his next
   instruction was about that page's contents.
4. **No message box on the setup page.** (2026-10-08)
5. **No smart wording that only a model could write.** The card's text comes
   from rules over OrcaSlicer's data. "8 mm outer brim" merges two settings and
   cannot be produced by a rule, so it is not shown. The agent's own chat
   message is where that sentence lives.

## The trap this handoff exists to avoid

An earlier agent produced a good-looking mockup with hand-written summary
text. At implementation there was no way to get from raw data to that text, so
the code fell back to a hard-coded field list (`kSetupKeys`, 13 keys). Kenneth
named this explicitly and asked that it not happen again.

How this handoff guards against it:

- Every string in `mockup.png` is one the rules below produce. Setting values
  are in the exact form `display_change` emits (already implemented and
  tested). Group captions are the real page and group names from OrcaSlicer's
  settings tabs.
- The acceptance tests include a random-settings test that a hard-coded list
  cannot pass.
- If you find a place where a rule cannot produce what the mockup shows, stop
  and report it. Do not special-case a setting to make the picture match.

## What exists today

Search by symbol; line numbers move.

| Thing | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| The card | `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx` | `appliedSummary` builds the two fixed lines; `Details` is the inline expansion; `SETTING_NAMES` names 14 keys and counts the rest. |
| Card styles | `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css`, classes `current-setup*` | Reused as they are. |
| The 13-key list | `kSetupKeys` and `applied_setup_of` in `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp` | To be removed. |
| Differences from the process preset | `preset_deltas_of` in the same file | Already generic over a `PresetCollection`, but the snapshot only calls it for the process preset. |
| What the page receives | `WorkspaceContext`, `PresetDeltaInfo`, `AppliedSetupInfo` in `AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts`; serialized in `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` (`send_context`) | |
| View switching | `App.tsx`, `const [view, setView] = useState<'chat' \| 'list' \| 'setup'>` | `'setup'` already means the agent's own setup screens. Pick a different name for the new view. |
| Setting definitions | `Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp` (after the patch) | `setting_definition`, `scope_definitions`. |
| Page and group of a setting | `Search::OptionsSearcher::get_option(opt_key, type)` in `src/slic3r/GUI/Search.hpp`, reached through `Plater::get_searcher()` | Returns `category` (the tab page) and `group`. Read the warning in step 3. |

## Work already done: apply `formatter.patch`

```bash
git apply /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/handoff-setup-card-differences/formatter.patch
```

The same files sit uncommitted in the worktree
`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/print-settings-display-a02cb1`.
Do not work in that worktree; create your own.

What the patch contains:

- `Workspace/SettingDisplay.hpp`: `display_value(definition, value)` and
  `display_change(definition, from, to)`. They turn OrcaSlicer's serialized
  value into display text using only the setting's type, unit and choice
  labels. No setting key appears in the file.
- `Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp`: the setting-definition helpers,
  moved unchanged out of `OrcaSettings.hpp` so code and tests with no GUI can
  use them.
- `tests/workspace/test_setting_display.cpp` and a `setting_display_tests`
  target. It links only `libslic3r`, so it builds in a few minutes in a fresh
  worktree.

What was verified: 2,635 assertions pass. One test runs the formatter over all
652 process, filament and printer settings and requires one line of at most 48
characters. That test was shown to fail when a rule was broken on purpose. The
two source files that include the split header still compile. Nothing calls
the formatter yet, and the full app was not built.

Rules the formatter applies:

| Type | Raw | Shown |
|---|---|---|
| Number with a unit | `0.28` | 0.28 mm |
| Percent | `15%` | 15% |
| Length or percent | `0.42` / `50%` | 0.42 mm / 50% |
| Switch | `1` / `0` | On / Off |
| Choice | `outer_only` | Outer brim only (OrcaSlicer's own label) |
| One value per filament, all equal | `220,220` | 220 ℃ |
| One value per filament, different | `0.4,0.6` | 0.4 mm, 0.6 mm |
| Unset entry | `nil` | Not set |
| Long or multi-line text | G-code | 3 lines |
| A change | `0` to `8` | 0 → 8 mm (unit said once) |

A hidden test prints a random 5% sample as a table, for review:

```bash
<build>/tests/workspace/RelWithDebInfo/setting_display_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/setting_display_tests "[.sample]" --rng-seed 7
```

## The design

![Mockup](mockup.png)

Frames in the picture: **A1** the card with changes, **A2** the card with
nothing changed and nothing sliced, **B** the setup page. Top row light, bottom
row dark. Each frame is 320 px wide, the panel's minimum width
(`component.agentPane.minWidth`), which is the worst case for fitting text.

### The card in the chat (A1, A2)

The card keeps its header, state label, estimate area, attention block,
working and saved-chat behaviour exactly as they are. Only the lines between
the title and the estimate change, and the "Setup details" toggle becomes a
link.

| Line | Rule | When absent |
|---|---|---|
| Title | The chat's recorded purpose (`setupIntent`); otherwise the full process preset name. Unchanged from today. | Never. |
| Presets line | Process preset and first filament preset, each cut at the first `" @"`, joined with `" · "`; `+N` after the filament when there are more filament slots. When the title is already the process preset, show the filaments only. | Non-FFF printer: omit. |
| Change rows | The first two differences from the presets, as `label` and `display_change` text. Order in the next section. | No differences: one line, "No changes from presets". |
| Count note | "N more changes" when there are more than two, and "N objects with overrides" when any object on the active plate has overrides, joined with `" · "`. | Both zero: omit. |
| Estimate and everything below | Unchanged. | |
| View setup | Opens the setup page. Replaces the "Setup details" toggle. | Never. |

The card never expands. Remove the inline `Details` block and the dimming of
the thread (`thread-dimmed`) that went with it.

Why the presets line is cut and has no printer: measured over every preset
shipped in `resources/profiles`, three full names joined are about 64
characters at the median and the card fits about 45. Process and filament cut
at `" @"` are about 33 at the median and 44 at the 90th percentile. The cut is
a naming convention (97% of process and 88% of filament presets follow it); a
name without `" @"` is shown whole and ends in an ellipsis if it overflows.
Full names are always on the setup page.

### Order of the change rows

1. Differences the agent made, then differences the person made
   (`PresetDeltaInfo.origin`, which exists today).
2. Within each, newest first. This needs the setting's key on the change log
   (see step 4). Where no change-log entry exists for a difference, use
   OrcaSlicer's own settings order (`Preset::print_options()` and its filament
   and printer equivalents), process before filament before printer.

### The setup page (B)

It replaces the chat body, like the chat list does. The message box is hidden.
"Back" returns to the chat. Sections, each present only when it has content:

| Section | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Header | The same label, state and title as the card. | As the card. |
| Presets | Printer, process, each filament slot, build plate, with full names. | `setupIdentity`, `printer.process`. All exist today. |
| Changed from presets · N | Grouped first by preset (its full name), then by "page · group" from OrcaSlicer's settings tabs, then one row per setting. | `presetDeltas`, extended in step 2 and 3. |
| Objects on \<plate\> · N | One line per printable object. An object with overrides is a disclosure that opens to rows grouped by what the override is on ("Whole object", "\<name\> · modifier"). An object without any reads "Uses plate settings". | `appliedSetup.objects`, `appliedSetup.localOverrides`, extended in step 5. |
| Plates | One row per plate: name, "shown" on the active one, and its estimate or "Not sliced". | `plates[]`. Exists today. |

A saved chat's page is built from that chat's saved summary, never from the
live project, exactly as the card is today.

### What makes the lines change

The lines are not stored. The host re-sends the context on every workspace
change and again after a successful agent settings change or title update
(`AgentHost`'s workspace and tool-activity subscriptions), and the page
rebuilds from it. So:

- The presets line changes when a different process or filament preset is
  selected, the printer is switched, a preset is saved under a new name, or a
  project is opened.
- The change rows change when a setting is edited by hand or by the agent,
  put back to the preset's value, restored by undo or redo, when the preset is
  saved with the edits in it, or when a different preset is selected.
- Selecting or moving objects and slicing change only the estimate. Switching
  plates changes the object-override count and the estimate.

## Styling contract: tokens only, nothing freehand

The design system is `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, applied to the
page as CSS variables by `WebShared/tokens.ts` and `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts`.
Read "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` before
touching any style. `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` fails the build on a literal
colour, radius or font in the stylesheet.

`mockup.html` was generated, not drawn: `make-mockup.py` writes the variables
from the token file with the same naming rules the page uses, includes
`AgentUI/src/styles.css` unedited, and adds the four new rules below. Running
it again reproduces the file byte for byte:

```bash
python3 make-mockup.py mockup.html <path to your checkout>
```

### Every element and the existing style it uses

| Element in the mockup | Existing class | Type role | Colour tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Card container | `.current-setup` | | `--surface-subtle`; `--radius-container` |
| Accent edge on a live card | `.current-setup--live` | | `--action-primary` |
| "Setup summary" / state | `.current-setup-header`, `-label`, `-state` | `--font-metadata-bold` | `--action-primary` live, `--text-secondary` otherwise |
| Title | `.current-setup-title` | `--font-body-bold` | `--text-primary` |
| Presets line, "No changes from presets", estimate sentence | `.current-setup-line` | `--font-label` | `--text-secondary` |
| A row: name left, value right | `.current-setup-rows`, `.current-setup-row` (`dt`, `dd`) | `--font-metadata` | `--text-secondary` name, `--text-primary` value |
| Count note, "Uses plate settings" | `.current-setup-note` | `--font-metadata` | `--text-secondary` |
| Time, material, plate | `.current-setup-metrics`, `-metric` | `--font-label-bold` | `--text-primary`; icons `--text-secondary` at `--setup-card-icon-size` |
| Divider | `.current-setup-divider` | | `--border-subtle` |
| "View setup", "Compute estimates" | `.current-setup-link` | `--font-label-bold` | `--action-primary`, `-hover`, `-pressed`; `--radius-standard` |
| Section heading ("Presets") | `.current-setup h3` inside `.current-setup-section` | `--font-label-bold` | `--text-secondary` |
| Preset name above its groups, object name | `.current-setup-object-name` | `--font-metadata-bold` | `--text-primary` |
| Object that opens | `.current-setup-disclosure` with `.jp-icon-chevron-down` / `-right` | `--font-label-bold` | `--text-secondary`; `--radius-standard`; icon `--button-icon-icon-size` |
| Page header bar | `.chat-header` | | `--surface-canvas`, `--border-subtle` |
| "Back" | `.printer-link-button.printer-back-link` with `.jp-icon-chevron-left` | `--font-label-bold` | `--action-primary` |
| Area around the card | `.pinned-setup` | | `--surface-canvas` |

Icons are the existing `jp-icon-*` masks: `clock`, `package`, `grid-3x3`,
`chevron-left`, `chevron-down`, `chevron-right`. No new icon.

"Back" borrows a class named for the printer panel. Give the rule a neutral
name shared by both uses; do not copy its declarations into a second rule.

### The four rules this design adds

They are in `mockup.html` under "Rules this design adds". Each uses only
existing variables and spacing from the 4-to-48 scale. No new token is needed.

| New class | Purpose | Declarations that carry a token or scale value |
|---|---|---|
| `.current-setup-page` | The page's scrolling body. | `padding: 12px`; `background: var(--surface-canvas)`. The same two values as `.pinned-setup`. |
| `.current-setup-group` | "Others · Brim" caption above a run of rows. | `font: var(--font-metadata-bold)`; `color: var(--text-secondary)`; `padding-top: 4px`. The same role and colour as `.current-setup-sent`. |
| `.current-setup-row--change` | Keeps a change row on one line: the name truncates with an ellipsis, the value is never cut. | Layout only (`flex`, `min-width`, `overflow`, `max-width: 60%`). The full name goes in the `title` attribute. |
| `.current-setup-object-rows` | Indents an opened object's rows under its name. | `padding-left: 24px` (icon 16 + gap 8); `gap: 4px`. |

New class names must start with `current-setup-`. The `setup-*` prefix belongs
to the agent's setup screens, the stylesheet is global, and a clash there once
broke layout with every test passing.

### Deliberately not in the design

- **No "agent" / "you" badge on a row.** An earlier sketch had one. The
  design system has no badge or tag component, so drawing one would be
  freehand. Who made a change is carried by the order of the rows. Adding a
  badge is a design decision for Kenneth.
- **No new colour, type size or radius.** If you believe you need one, stop
  and ask. Do not add a token on your own for this work.

## Implementation steps

Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `architecture.md` and, before any edit
outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, `fork-stewardship.md`. Nothing below needs
a change to an OrcaSlicer-owned file; if you find one that does, stop and
report it with the reason.

1. **Apply `formatter.patch`.** Build and run `setting_display_tests`.
2. **Send differences for all three preset types.** In the workspace
   snapshot, call `preset_deltas_of` for the edited filament preset and the
   edited printer preset as well as the process preset. Add to each
   difference: which preset type it belongs to, that preset's name, and the
   `display_change` text. Keep the raw `preset` and `value` fields.
3. **Add the page and group of each setting.** Look each key up in
   OrcaSlicer's search index (`Search::OptionsSearcher::get_option`).
   **Warning:** when a key is not in the index, for example because the
   current user mode hides it, that function returns some other option
   instead of failing. Compare the returned option's key with the one you
   asked for, and send no page or group when they differ. Also check what it
   returns for per-filament keys, which the index stores with a `#0` suffix.
   This lookup has been read in the source but never run; verify it in the
   running app before building on it.
4. **Put the setting's key on the change log.** `WorkspaceEdit` and
   `ChangeInfo` carry a label, and labels are not unique (17 process labels
   are shared; "Outer wall" names four settings). Add the key as an optional
   field so the card can order differences newest first.
5. **Name every override.** For each entry in `local_overrides`, send the
   setting's label and `display_value` text. The card then stops using
   `SETTING_NAMES`, and "N other local settings" disappears because every
   setting now has a name.
6. **Remove the fixed list.** Delete `kSetupKeys`, the `settings` array it
   fills, and `appliedSummary`, `appliedRows`, `clause` and their helpers in
   the card. Before deleting, confirm nothing else reads `settings`: at
   `e3f826a83c` the only readers were the adapter, `AgentHost`'s serializer,
   the card, and tests.
7. **Rebuild the card and add the page** to the rules and styles above. Add a
   view to `App.tsx`'s switch, hide the message box on it, and return to the
   chat on "Back", on a project change, and when the panel is told to focus a
   chat (the two existing effects that call `setView('chat')`).
8. **Update fixtures and tests** (`SetupCard.visual-cases.tsx`,
   `SetupCard.test.tsx`, `SetupCard.acceptance.test.tsx`, `App.test.tsx`,
   `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp`).

### Protocol rules

- Every new field is optional. Do not raise the bridge protocol version;
  additive changes use the capabilities list.
- Saved chats written before this change have none of the new fields. The
  card must still draw them: show `label` with the raw `preset → value` as the
  list does today, no group caption, and ignore a saved `settings` array.
  Never fill a saved card from today's project.

## Known rough edges. Report them; do not paper over them.

Found by running the formatter over real settings:

- **A zero often means "off" or "automatic".** "Internal solid infill: 0" and
  "0 layers" are accurate and unhelpful. The definitions do not record what
  zero means. Leave these as they are. Do not add per-setting wording.
- **Two settings can share a label and a unit.** "Brim width" is both the
  brim's and the prime tower's. On the setup page the group caption separates
  them ("Others · Brim" against "Multimaterial · Prime tower"). On the card
  there is no caption, so put "page · group · label" in the row's tooltip.
- **Some labels are long.** One is 62 characters. The truncation rule and the
  tooltip handle it.
- **OrcaSlicer's own category field is often empty.** It was blank for 18 of
  33 sampled settings, which is why grouping uses the search index.
- **An object's filament choice.** The `extruder` override holds a slot
  number. Today the card rewrites it as "Filament N · \<preset\>". That is the
  one place a key is named. Either keep that single documented exception or
  show the number; say which you chose.
- **Spiral vase mode** can be set on a plate without being a preset
  difference. Show it in that plate's row on the setup page.

## Choices made while writing this handoff that Kenneth has not confirmed

Implement them as written, and list them in your report so he can overrule
any of them:

1. Two change rows on the card. He saw this in a text sketch and did not
   object; three items on one line were measured not to fit.
2. With no recorded purpose, the title is the process preset and the presets
   line shows filaments only.
3. The wording "View setup", "Back", "No changes from presets", "N more
   changes", "N objects with overrides", "Uses plate settings".
4. The Plates section shows only each plate's estimate or "Not sliced".
5. No row badge for who made a change.

## Relationship to the earlier handoff and to Figma

`../handoff-setup-summary-card/` (2026-10-05) specified the card that exists
now. It stays in force for the title, the estimate area, attention findings,
card states, saved-chat behaviour and its truthfulness rules. This handoff
supersedes its "short applied-settings summary" (the fixed fields) and its
inline expandable details.

The Figma page "Current Setup Card" (sections 5 to 7) still shows the old
summary lines and the inline expansion. For those two parts this folder's
mockup is the source. Do not edit Figma; tell Kenneth it is out of date so he
can decide how to update it.

## Acceptance

Done means all of these, demonstrated and reported with their output:

1. **Random settings test.** In the page's tests, generate differences for
   five settings chosen at random from all process, filament and printer
   settings, on several seeds, and assert every one appears on the setup page
   with a non-empty label and value, and that the card shows two and counts
   three more.
2. **No setting key in the card.** A test fails if `SetupCard.tsx` or the new
   page's source contains a config key. If you keep the `extruder` exception,
   it is the only allowed entry and is listed in the test. Prove the test can
   fail by adding a key and watching it fail.
3. **Host test.** For every setting in each preset type, a difference built
   from it carries a `display_change` text; a key missing from the search
   index yields no group and no wrong group.
4. **Saved chats.** A context without the new fields renders with raw values
   and no error.
5. **Guards.** `setting_display_tests`, `workspace_contract_tests`,
   `brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`.
6. **Visual check against the mockup.** Add fixture cases for A1, A2 and B to
   `SetupCard.visual-cases.tsx`, render them in light and dark at 320 px, and
   compare with `mockup.png`. Then repeat with a long label, a long preset
   name without `" @"`, six filaments, and twenty differences.
7. **Live check in the built app**, with an isolated data directory: change a
   process setting by hand and see the row appear; set it back and see it go;
   edit a filament temperature and see it under the filament's name; save the
   preset and see "No changes from presets"; undo an agent change; open the
   setup page, switch plates, go back. Build `jusprin_web` after every page
   edit or the app loads the old bundle.

Do not claim a step is verified if it was only compiled. If something cannot
be tested, say which and why.

input.content:
# Handoff: setup card shows differences from presets

Prepared 2026-10-08 at commit `e3f826a83c`, branch
`claude/print-settings-display-a02cb1`.

This folder is a temporary implementation handoff. Leave it untracked: do not
commit it and do not add it to any ignore file.

## The assignment in three sentences

The setup summary card in the Agent panel currently describes a print with a
fixed list of 13 slicer settings, so it shows wall loops to someone who asked
about bed adhesion and can never show a setting outside that list. Replace
that with one rule that covers every setting: the card shows which presets are
selected and what differs from them. The long expandable details move out of
the chat onto a separate page inside the panel, so the card never pushes the
conversation down.

## Files in this folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | This document. |
| `mockup.png` | The three screens, in light and dark, rendered from `mockup.html`. Look at this first. |
| `mockup.html` | Self-contained mockup. Open in a browser to inspect elements and classes. |
| `make-mockup.py` | The script that generated `mockup.html` from the token file and the page's stylesheet. |
| `formatter.patch` | Work already done and tested: the generic value formatter and its tests. Apply it first. |

## Decisions Kenneth has made. Do not reopen them.

1. **No hard-coded setting list.** (2026-10-07) The two summary lines must not
   be fixed fields. He called the current behaviour arbitrary.
2. **The card means "differs from the preset".** (2026-10-08) Not "changed in
   this chat". A consequence he accepted: saving a preset with the edits in it
   empties the list, because nothing differs any more.
3. **Details are a page inside the panel, not an inline expansion.** He asked
   whether it should be a page or a popup; a page was recommended and his next
   instruction was about that page's contents.
4. **No message box on the setup page.** (2026-10-08)
5. **No smart wording that only a model could write.** The card's text comes
   from rules over OrcaSlicer's data. "8 mm outer brim" merges two settings and
   cannot be produced by a rule, so it is not shown. The agent's own chat
   message is where that sentence lives.

## The trap this handoff exists to avoid

An earlier agent produced a good-looking mockup with hand-written summary
text. At implementation there was no way to get from raw data to that text, so
the code fell back to a hard-coded field list (`kSetupKeys`, 13 keys). Kenneth
named this explicitly and asked that it not happen again.

How this handoff guards against it:

- Every string in `mockup.png` is one the rules below produce. Setting values
  are in the exact form `display_change` emits (already implemented and
  tested). Group captions are the real page and group names from OrcaSlicer's
  settings tabs. The one free-text string is the title "Stop the corners
  lifting", which stands for a purpose the agent recorded; that field exists
  today.
- The acceptance tests include a random-settings test that a hard-coded list
  cannot pass.
- If you find a place where a rule cannot produce what the mockup shows, stop
  and report it. Do not special-case a setting to make the picture match.

## What exists today

Search by symbol; line numbers move.

| Thing | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| The card | `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx` | `appliedSummary` builds the two fixed lines; `Details` is the inline expansion; `SETTING_NAMES` names 14 keys and counts the rest. |
| Card styles | `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css`, classes `current-setup*` | Reused as they are. |
| The 13-key list | `kSetupKeys` and `applied_setup_of` in `Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp` | To be removed. |
| Differences from the process preset | `preset_deltas_of` in the same file | Already generic over a `PresetCollection`, but the snapshot only calls it for the process preset. |
| What the page receives | `WorkspaceContext`, `PresetDeltaInfo`, `AppliedSetupInfo` in `AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts`; serialized in `Agent/AgentHost.cpp` (`send_context`) | |
| View switching | `App.tsx`, `const [view, setView] = useState<'chat' \| 'list' \| 'setup'>` | `'setup'` already means the agent's own setup screens. Pick a different name for the new view. |
| Setting definitions | `Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp` (after the patch) | `setting_definition`, `scope_definitions`. |
| Page and group of a setting | `Search::OptionsSearcher::get_option(opt_key, type)` in `src/slic3r/GUI/Search.hpp`, reached through `Plater::get_searcher()` | Returns `category` (the tab page) and `group`. Read the warning in step 3. |

## Work already done: apply `formatter.patch`

Create your own worktree; do not work in this one. Then:

```bash
git apply /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/print-settings-display-a02cb1/handoff-setup-card-differences/formatter.patch
```

The patch is the uncommitted state of this worktree at `e3f826a83c`.

What the patch contains:

- `Workspace/SettingDisplay.hpp`: `display_value(definition, value)` and
  `display_change(definition, from, to)`. They turn OrcaSlicer's serialized
  value into display text using only the setting's type, unit and choice
  labels. No setting key appears in the file.
- `Workspace/OrcaSettingDefinitions.hpp`: the setting-definition helpers,
  moved unchanged out of `OrcaSettings.hpp` so code and tests with no GUI can
  use them.
- `tests/workspace/test_setting_display.cpp` and a `setting_display_tests`
  target. It links only `libslic3r`, so it builds in a few minutes in a fresh
  worktree.

What was verified: 2,635 assertions pass. One test runs the formatter over all
652 process, filament and printer settings and requires one line of at most 48
characters. That test was shown to fail when a rule was broken on purpose. The
two source files that include the split header still compile. Nothing calls
the formatter yet, and the full app was not built.

Rules the formatter applies:

| Type | Raw | Shown |
|---|---|---|
| Number with a unit | `0.28` | 0.28 mm |
| Percent | `15%` | 15% |
| Length or percent | `0.42` / `50%` | 0.42 mm / 50% |
| Switch | `1` / `0` | On / Off |
| Choice | `outer_only` | Outer brim only (OrcaSlicer's own label) |
| One value per filament, all equal | `220,220` | 220 ℃ |
| One value per filament, different | `0.4,0.6` | 0.4 mm, 0.6 mm |
| Unset entry | `nil` | Not set |
| Long or multi-line text | G-code | 3 lines |
| A change | `0` to `8` | 0 → 8 mm (unit said once) |

A hidden test prints a random 5% sample as a table, for review:

```bash
<build>/tests/workspace/RelWithDebInfo/setting_display_tests.app/Contents/MacOS/setting_display_tests "[.sample]" --rng-seed 7
```

## The design

![Mockup](mockup.png)

Frames in the picture: **A1** the card with changes, **A2** the card with
nothing changed and nothing sliced, **B** the setup page. Top row light, bottom
row dark. Each frame is 320 px wide, the panel's minimum width
(`component.agentPane.minWidth`), which is the worst case for fitting text.

### The card in the chat (A1, A2)

The card keeps its header, state label, estimate area, attention block,
working and saved-chat behaviour exactly as they are. Only the lines between
the title and the estimate change, and the "Setup details" toggle becomes a
link.

| Line | Rule | When absent |
|---|---|---|
| Title | The chat's recorded purpose (`setupIntent`); otherwise the full process preset name. Unchanged from today. | Never. |
| Presets line | Process preset and first filament preset, each cut at the first `" @"`, joined with `" · "`; `+N` after the filament when there are more filament slots. When the title is already the process preset, show the filaments only. | Non-FFF printer: omit. |
| Change rows | The first two differences from the presets, as `label` and `display_change` text. Order in the next section. | No differences: one line, "No changes from presets". |
| Count note | "N more changes" when there are more than two, and "N objects with overrides" when any object on the active plate has overrides, joined with `" · "`. | Both zero: omit. |
| Estimate and everything below | Unchanged. | |
| View setup | Opens the setup page. Replaces the "Setup details" toggle. | Never. |

The card never expands. Remove the inline `Details` block and the dimming of
the thread (`thread-dimmed`) that went with it.

Why the presets line is cut and has no printer: measured over every preset
shipped in `resources/profiles`, three full names joined are about 64
characters at the median and the card fits about 45. Process and filament cut
at `" @"` are about 33 at the median and 44 at the 90th percentile. The cut is
a naming convention (97% of process and 88% of filament presets follow it); a
name without `" @"` is shown whole and ends in an ellipsis if it overflows.
Full names are always on the setup page.

### Order of the change rows

1. Differences the agent made, then differences the person made
   (`PresetDeltaInfo.origin`, which exists today).
2. Within each, newest first. This needs the setting's key on the change log
   (see step 4). Where no change-log entry exists for a difference, use
   OrcaSlicer's own settings order (`Preset::print_options()` and its filament
   and printer equivalents), process before filament before printer.

### The setup page (B)

It replaces the chat body, like the chat list does. The message box is hidden.
"Back" returns to the chat. Sections, each present only when it has content:

| Section | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Header | The same label, state and title as the card. | As the card. |
| Presets | Printer, process, each filament slot, build plate, with full names. | `setupIdentity`, `printer.process`. All exist today. |
| Changed from presets · N | Grouped first by preset (its full name), then by "page · group" from OrcaSlicer's settings tabs, then one row per setting. | `presetDeltas`, extended in steps 2 and 3. |
| Objects on \<plate\> · N | One line per printable object. An object with overrides is a disclosure that opens to rows grouped by what the override is on ("Whole object", "\<name\> · modifier"). An object without any reads "Uses plate settings". | `appliedSetup.objects`, `appliedSetup.localOverrides`, extended in step 5. |
| Plates | One row per plate: name, "shown" on the active one, and its estimate or "Not sliced". | `plates[]`. Exists today. |

A saved chat's page is built from that chat's saved summary, never from the
live project, exactly as the card is today.

### What makes the lines change

The lines are not stored. The host re-sends the context on every workspace
change and again after a successful agent settings change or title update
(`AgentHost`'s workspace and tool-activity subscriptions), and the page
rebuilds from it. So:

- The presets line changes when a different process or filament preset is
  selected, the printer is switched, a preset is saved under a new name, or a
  project is opened.
- The change rows change when a setting is edited by hand or by the agent,
  put back to the preset's value, restored by undo or redo, when the preset is
  saved with the edits in it, or when a different preset is selected.
- Selecting or moving objects and slicing change only the estimate. Switching
  plates changes the object-override count and the estimate.

## Styling contract: tokens only, nothing freehand

The design system is `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, applied to the
page as CSS variables by `WebShared/tokens.ts` and `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts`.
Read "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` before
touching any style. `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` fails the build on a literal
colour, radius or font in the stylesheet.

`mockup.html` was generated, not drawn: `make-mockup.py` writes the variables
from the token file with the same naming rules the page uses, includes
`AgentUI/src/styles.css` unedited, and adds the four new rules below. Running
it again reproduces the file byte for byte:

```bash
python3 make-mockup.py mockup.html <path to your checkout>
```

### Every element and the existing style it uses

| Element in the mockup | Existing class | Type role | Colour and shape tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Card container | `.current-setup` | | `--surface-subtle`; `--radius-container` |
| Accent edge on a live card | `.current-setup--live` | | `--action-primary` |
| "Setup summary" / state | `.current-setup-header`, `-label`, `-state` | `--font-metadata-bold` | `--action-primary` live, `--text-secondary` otherwise |
| Title | `.current-setup-title` | `--font-body-bold` | `--text-primary` |
| Presets line, "No changes from presets", estimate sentence | `.current-setup-line` | `--font-label` | `--text-secondary` |
| A row: name left, value right | `.current-setup-rows`, `.current-setup-row` (`dt`, `dd`) | `--font-metadata` | `--text-secondary` name, `--text-primary` value |
| Count note, "Uses plate settings" | `.current-setup-note` | `--font-metadata` | `--text-secondary` |
| Time, material, plate | `.current-setup-metrics`, `-metric` | `--font-label-bold` | `--text-primary`; icons `--text-secondary` at `--setup-card-icon-size` |
| Divider | `.current-setup-divider` | | `--border-subtle` |
| "View setup", "Compute estimates" | `.current-setup-link` | `--font-label-bold` | `--action-primary`, `-hover`, `-pressed`; `--radius-standard` |
| Section heading ("Presets") | `.current-setup h3` inside `.current-setup-section` | `--font-label-bold` | `--text-secondary` |
| Preset name above its groups, object name | `.current-setup-object-name` | `--font-metadata-bold` | `--text-primary` |
| Object that opens | `.current-setup-disclosure` with `.jp-icon-chevron-down` / `-right` | `--font-label-bold` | `--text-secondary`; `--radius-standard`; icon `--button-icon-icon-size` |
| Page header bar | `.chat-header` | | `--surface-canvas`, `--border-subtle` |
| "Back" | `.printer-link-button.printer-back-link` with `.jp-icon-chevron-left` | `--font-label-bold` | `--action-primary` |
| Area around the card | `.pinned-setup` | | `--surface-canvas` |

Icons are the existing `jp-icon-*` masks: `clock`, `package`, `grid-3x3`,
`chevron-left`, `chevron-down`, `chevron-right`. No new icon.

"Back" borrows a class named for the printer panel. Give the rule a neutral
name shared by both uses; do not copy its declarations into a second rule.

### The four rules this design adds

They are in `mockup.html` under "Rules this design adds". Each uses only
existing variables and spacing from the 4-to-48 scale. No new token is needed.

| New class | Purpose | Declarations that carry a token or scale value |
|---|---|---|
| `.current-setup-page` | The page's scrolling body. | `padding: 12px`; `background: var(--surface-canvas)`. The same two values as `.pinned-setup`. |
| `.current-setup-group` | "Others · Brim" caption above a run of rows. | `font: var(--font-metadata-bold)`; `color: var(--text-secondary)`; `padding-top: 4px`. The same role and colour as `.current-setup-sent`. |
| `.current-setup-row--change` | Keeps a change row on one line: the name truncates with an ellipsis, the value is never cut. | Layout only (`flex`, `min-width`, `overflow`, `max-width: 60%`). The full name goes in the `title` attribute. |
| `.current-setup-object-rows` | Indents an opened object's rows under its name. | `padding-left: 24px` (icon 16 + gap 8); `gap: 4px`. |

New class names must start with `current-setup-`. The `setup-*` prefix belongs
to the agent's setup screens, the stylesheet is global, and a clash there once
broke layout with every test passing.

### Deliberately not in the design

- **No "agent" / "you" badge on a row.** An earlier sketch had one. The
  design system has no badge or tag component, so drawing one would be
  freehand. Who made a change is carried by the order of the rows. Adding a
  badge is a design decision for Kenneth.
- **No new colour, type size or radius.** If you believe you need one, stop
  and ask. Do not add a token on your own for this work.

## Implementation steps

Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `architecture.md` and, before any edit
outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, `fork-stewardship.md`. Nothing below needs
a change to an OrcaSlicer-owned file; if you find one that does, stop and
report it with the reason.

1. **Apply `formatter.patch`.** Build and run `setting_display_tests`.
2. **Send differences for all three preset types.** In the workspace
   snapshot, call `preset_deltas_of` for the edited filament preset and the
   edited printer preset as well as the process preset. Add to each
   difference: which preset type it belongs to, that preset's name, and the
   `display_change` text. Keep the raw `preset` and `value` fields.
3. **Add the page and group of each setting.** Look each key up in
   OrcaSlicer's search index (`Search::OptionsSearcher::get_option`).
   **Warning:** when a key is not in the index, for example because the
   current user mode hides it, that function returns some other option
   instead of failing. Compare the returned option's key with the one you
   asked for, and send no page or group when they differ. Also check what it
   returns for per-filament keys, which the index stores with a `#0` suffix.
   This lookup has been read in the source but never run; verify it in the
   running app before building on it.
4. **Put the setting's key on the change log.** `WorkspaceEdit` and
   `ChangeInfo` carry a label, and labels are not unique (17 process labels
   are shared; "Outer wall" names four settings). Add the key as an optional
   field so the card can order differences newest first.
5. **Name every override.** For each entry in `local_overrides`, send the
   setting's label and `display_value` text. The card then stops using
   `SETTING_NAMES`, and "N other local settings" disappears because every
   setting now has a name.
6. **Remove the fixed list.** Delete `kSetupKeys`, the `settings` array it
   fills, and `appliedSummary`, `appliedRows`, `clause` and their helpers in
   the card. Before deleting, confirm nothing else reads `settings`: at
   `e3f826a83c` the only readers were the adapter, `AgentHost`'s serializer,
   the card, and tests.
7. **Rebuild the card and add the page** to the rules and styles above. Add a
   view to `App.tsx`'s switch, hide the message box on it, and return to the
   chat on "Back", on a project change, and when the panel is told to focus a
   chat (the two existing effects that call `setView('chat')`).
8. **Update fixtures and tests** (`SetupCard.visual-cases.tsx`,
   `SetupCard.test.tsx`, `SetupCard.acceptance.test.tsx`, `App.test.tsx`,
   `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp`).

### Protocol rules

- Every new field is optional. Do not raise the bridge protocol version;
  additive changes use the capabilities list.
- Saved chats written before this change have none of the new fields. The
  card must still draw them: show `label` with the raw `preset → value` as the
  list does today, no group caption, and ignore a saved `settings` array.
  Never fill a saved card from today's project.

## Known rough edges. Report them; do not paper over them.

Found by running the formatter over real settings:

- **A zero often means "off" or "automatic".** "Internal solid infill: 0" and
  "0 layers" are accurate and unhelpful. The definitions do not record what
  zero means. Leave these as they are. Do not add per-setting wording.
- **Two settings can share a label and a unit.** "Brim width" is both the
  brim's and the prime tower's. On the setup page the group caption separates
  them ("Others · Brim" against "Multimaterial · Prime tower"). On the card
  there is no caption, so put "page · group · label" in the row's tooltip.
- **Some labels are long.** One is 62 characters. The truncation rule and the
  tooltip handle it.
- **OrcaSlicer's own category field is often empty.** It was blank for 18 of
  33 sampled settings, which is why grouping uses the search index.
- **An object's filament choice.** The `extruder` override holds a slot
  number. Today the card rewrites it as "Filament N · \<preset\>". That is the
  one place a key is named. Either keep that single documented exception or
  show the number; say which you chose.
- **Spiral vase mode** can be set on a plate without being a preset
  difference. Show it in that plate's row on the setup page.

## Choices made while writing this handoff that Kenneth has not confirmed

Implement them as written, and list them in your report so he can overrule
any of them:

1. Two change rows on the card. He saw this in a text sketch and did not
   object; three items on one line were measured not to fit.
2. With no recorded purpose, the title is the process preset and the presets
   line shows filaments only.
3. The wording "View setup", "Back", "No changes from presets", "N more
   changes", "N objects with overrides", "Uses plate settings".
4. The Plates section shows only each plate's estimate or "Not sliced".
5. No row badge for who made a change.
6. The page has no title of its own in the header bar, only "Back".

## Relationship to the earlier handoff and to Figma

`/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/handoff-setup-summary-card/` (2026-10-05)
specified the card that exists now. It stays in force for the title, the
estimate area, attention findings, card states, saved-chat behaviour and its
truthfulness rules. This handoff supersedes its "short applied-settings
summary" (the fixed fields) and its inline expandable details.

The Figma page "Current Setup Card" (sections 5 to 7) still shows the old
summary lines and the inline expansion. For those two parts this folder's
mockup is the source. Do not edit Figma; tell Kenneth it is out of date so he
can decide how to update it.

## Acceptance

Done means all of these, demonstrated and reported with their output:

1. **Random settings test.** In the page's tests, generate differences for
   five settings chosen at random from all process, filament and printer
   settings, on several seeds, and assert every one appears on the setup page
   with a non-empty label and value, and that the card shows two and counts
   three more.
2. **No setting key in the card.** A test fails if `SetupCard.tsx` or the new
   page's source contains a config key. If you keep the `extruder` exception,
   it is the only allowed entry and is listed in the test. Prove the test can
   fail by adding a key and watching it fail.
3. **Host test.** For every setting in each preset type, a difference built
   from it carries a `display_change` text; a key missing from the search

content.text:
The handoff for the setup summary card is written. It tells another agent to replace the card's fixed list of 13 settings with "which presets are selected and what differs from them", and to move the long details onto a separate page inside the Agent panel. The mockup in it was generated by a script from the design token file and the page's real stylesheet, so no colour, font, radius or size was typed by hand.

## Where it is

The folder is [handoff-setup-card-differences](handoff-setup-card-differences/), untracked, in this session's worktree. Your other handoffs sit in the main checkout, but a safety hook blocks this session from writing there, so you may want to move it.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [README.md](handoff-setup-card-differences/README.md) | The handoff: your decisions, the rules for every line, the styling contract, eight implementation steps, acceptance tests. |
| [mockup.png](handoff-setup-card-differences/mockup.png) | Three screens in light and dark at 320 px, the panel's minimum width. |
| [mockup.html](handoff-setup-card-differences/mockup.html) | The same mockup, inspectable in a browser. |
| [make-mockup.py](handoff-setup-card-differences/make-mockup.py) | The generator. I confirmed it reproduces the mockup byte for byte. |
| [formatter.patch](handoff-setup-card-differences/formatter.patch) | The formatter and its tests from earlier, still uncommitted. I confirmed it applies to a clean checkout of `e3f826a83c`. |

## How the styling is pinned down

- **Existing styles:** the handoff has a table mapping every element in the mockup to the existing `current-setup-*` class it uses, with that class's type role and colour tokens.
- **New styles:** the design adds four CSS rules, all layout or existing variables. No new token is needed.
- **Strings:** every setting value is in the form the tested formatter emits, and the group captions ("Others · Brim") are the real page and group names from OrcaSlicer's settings tabs.

## Changes from the earlier sketch

- **No "agent" / "you" badge on rows.** The design system has no badge component, so drawing one would have been freehand. The row order carries who made the change.
- **Group captions come from OrcaSlicer's settings search index.** It maps each setting to its tab page and group, which separates the two "Brim width" settings. I read this in the source but did not run it. The handoff flags that, along with a trap: a failed lookup returns a different setting, not an error.
- **Newest-first ordering needs a small addition.** The change log records a setting's label, not its key, and labels are not unique. The handoff adds the key as an optional field.

## For you to check

- **Unconfirmed choices.** The handoff lists six choices I made that you have not confirmed, such as two change rows on the card and the wording "View setup". The implementer is told to build them as written and report them back.
- **Figma is out of date.** The "Current Setup Card" page still shows the old summary lines and inline expansion. The handoff tells the implementer not to edit Figma and to leave that update to you.
- **Nothing is committed.** If you want the formatter on the branch so the next agent can start from a commit instead of the patch, say so and I will commit it.
